newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Deer Farms call off public float - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: NZ Deer Farms call off public float - NZPA.

text.p: New Zealand Deer Farms has decided not to proceed with a public float, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.

Deer Farms, owned by interests associated with Dunedin businessmen Howard Paterson and David Smallbone, was reported to be contemplating a NZ$20 million float in March and a prospectus was expected to be issued today,
However, chairman Phil Pryke issued a statement saying recent market weakness meant conditions were no longer appropriate for such a public offer.
The decision on the public float would not affect the company's expansion.
"Several large private and corporate investors have expressed strong interest in the company and the offer has been restructured as a private placement of equity," he said.
NZ Deer Farms would continue to acquire farm properties in the Southland area in the next two years.
Pryke had earlier said the company owned three "very large" farms in the South Island and a substantial amount of stock.
"We have agreements in place for the purchase of a further number of farms over the next 18 months or so."
